newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan urges focus on May 30 Liberia elections.
newsitem.headline: Annan urges focus on May 30 Liberia elections.

text.p: Prospects for peace in Liberia seem more promising than at any time since the outbreak of a multi-sided civil war in December 1989, Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Monday, adding that efforts should now focus on elections set for May 30.
The elections are a key element of a peace accord signed at Abuja, Nigeria, last August after more than a dozen previous agreements broke down.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in the civil war, which has devastated Liberia's mining and rubber economy.

In a report to the Security Council, Annan recommended a three-month extension, until June 30, of the 92-member U.N. Observer Mission in Liberia (UNOMIL), which works with a 10,000-strong peacekeeping force called ECOMOG fielded by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

"Whereas much remains to be done and it is essential to remain alert to the dangers that still persist, the prospects for peace in Liberia now seems to be more promising than at any time since the start of the civil war," he said.
"The main focus of UNOMIL must now be the forthcoming elections," he said, concurring with arrangements for the voting recommended by an ECOWAS committee.

UNOMIL would help observe and verify this final stage of the Abuja peace plan. To ensure voters received neutral, factual information about the electoral process, Annan also recommended that UNOMIL be authorised to make arrangements for the production and broadcast of daily radio programmes.

The election will be organised and conducted by an independent elections commission comprising seven Liberian citizens -- three to be appointed by the former warring factions and four from civil society.
The parliament to be elected will comprise a 64-member House of Assembly and a 26-member Senate. Voting will be on the basis of proportional representation.

"ECOMOG is the key to the provision of adequate security for the elections," the U.N. chief said, appealing for donor countries to provide the force with assistance in transportation, petroleum products, communications, medical needs and anti-riot equipment.

Noting ECOMOG intended to begin withdrawing six months after the elections, he said it had proposed the start of a process for restructuring the Liberian armed forces, police and other security agencies, with assistance from the United Nations and the international community.
"I consider this an essential peace-building step which should help the incoming government build on the progress made in the last few months," Annan said.
